utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning to everyone in and around this courtroom. Madam Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is case IT-03-69-T, the Prosecutor versus Jovica Stanisic and Franko Simatovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. If there are no procedural matters to be raised, we'll move into closed session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in closed session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. May the witness be brought into the courtroom. Mr. Bakrac, you needed a couple of more minutes to conclude your cross-examination. Is that --

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. You're right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning, Witness DST-063. I hope you feel better by now.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I do. And I would like to seize this opportunity to apologise to everyone for the fact that I was unable to appear for my testimony on the scheduled day.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Since we understood that it was due to your medical condition, there's even no need to apologise, because you -- it goes without saying that you are excused during the time that you do not feel well. If there -- at any moment you would think that you, again, do not feel well, please inform me so that we can take appropriate action. I further would like to remind you that you're still bound by the solemn declaration you've given at the beginning of your testimony, that is, that you'll speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth. Mr. Bakrac will now continue his cross-examination. Mr. Bakrac, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. Good morning to everyone in and around the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Witness. Let us resume our examination. I have two more documents to show to you, and I'd like to have your comments on them.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we call up in e-court Exhibit D201.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Mr. Witness, while we're waiting for it to appear, let me tell you that it appears that the document is a report on the application of operative and technical equipment in respect of an individual. Let's look at page 1. The heading reads: "The Republic of Serbia, Ministry of the Interior, State Security Department, the State Security Department's centre of Novi Sad." And while we're on page one, let's establish the following. You do know how these documents were made. Can we agree that this has to do with the surveillance of an individual, according to standard procedure, between 7 and 16 November. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: DST-063 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now turn to the last page so that we can look at the signature of the operative involved.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: I'm sure you would be familiar with the individual, since he worked for the Novi Sad centre. Can you see it reads "Operative Slavko Vojvodic" and his signature. First of all, let us establish if you know this individual, Slavko Vojvodic.

utterances.speaker: DST-063 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Did he work for the State Security Department, specifically the Novi Sad centre, and which specific section?

utterances.speaker: DST-063 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. He did work at the Novi Sad centre of the RDB, and it was the third line of work, as it were.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: When you say "the third line of work," what does it mean specifically? What were they occupied with?

utterances.speaker: DST-063 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I think the heading itself stated extremism. In other words, internal matters. Domestic matters.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now turn to page 3. I think the corresponding page in English is 3 as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Have a look at the second paragraph. On the 12th of November, 1992, the source told us that at Kajmak, in inverted commas, Zivojin Ivanovic was present, in brackets, supposedly a member of the DB from Republika Srpska, who asked that -- who asked for people to fight in Herzegovina. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: DST-063 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: So if my understanding is correct, the operative work, which was in fact the surveillance of telephone contacts, was Kajmak, and Zivojin Ivanovic is supposedly a member of the DB from Republika Srpska. Or at least that's what the operative producing the report believed or that's how he introduced himself. Is my understanding of this operative's report correct in this respect?

utterances.speaker: DST-063 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Let's look at another report by the same individual but at a later date. I deliberately drew your attention to this specific paragraph where the operative states that Zivojin Ivanovic introduced himself and that it was assumed that he was a DB member from Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now look at D200.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: And while we're waiting, witness, let me tell you that this is the same sort of document, produced by the same individual, and it also involves the surveillance of one Kajmak but the date is the 4th of January, 1993. In other words, a month and a half later. Apparently Kajmak is being listened in to again, and I'm sure that you'll believe me if I tell you, and so will the OTP, that on page -- on the last page we have Slavko Vojvodic, the same operative's, signature. Now, let's look at page 3, paragraph 1. That's the top of page 3.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we have page 3 in B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: I'll read the relevant part and put my question to you then. Zivojin Ivanovic, a member of the DB of Krajina, told Kajmak that he was leaving for Kosovo, et cetera. This is my question: We were able to see that your colleague Slavko Vojvodic stated in November, said that Zivojin Ivanovic was supposedly a member of the DB of Republika Srpska; whereas in this report the reference to the same individual is that he was a member of the DB of Krajina but without the inverted commas? Now, you, as a person who knew this operative and knew how the Novi Sad centre worked, do you believe that an operative would write in no uncertain terms that an individual belonged to the DB of Krajina if he had not, in the previous month and a half, done something to ascertain that this was, indeed, the fact?

utterances.speaker: DST-063 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I'm sure that he would not have made a qualification of any sort had he not been certain of it to a certain extent.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: If my understanding of what you're saying is correct, in November he placed his qualification in brackets, saying a member of the DB of Republika Srpska, and this was in November of 1992, whereas in January of 1993, he wrote without the brackets that he was a member of the DB Krajina. Does this not mean that he checked the information in the meantime to make sure?

utterances.speaker: DST-063 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the time-frame involved certainly allows for such information to be checked up on.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Thank you. I have one more question left.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Bakrac, in relation to the last two documents you presented to the witness, if there's any issue - and you refer to it several times - that names are in between quotation marks or inverted commas, then, of course, in order to follow all that, the translation should also reflect that. Now, the translation does not in any way reflect any inverted commas in the original. So, therefore, since it apparently is an issue in dispute between Defence and Prosecution and where the Prosecution -- it's not quite clear to me, but suggests or makes an inference that it has some meaning, then it should at least be in the translation as well. So, therefore, I would like the translations to be verified on the use of inverted commas in relation to names and then to be uploaded again in e-court. I take it that the parties would agree with that.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, we agree with that.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. Let me just explain that our question at this point in time focussed on an individual whose name was not in inverted commas. But I do agree with you that that should be remedied.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Whether the specific questions dealt with that, it is a point that is in issue, and therefore the translation should reflect it so as to be able to further analyse the position of both parties.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I just wanted to raise another issue regarding Mr. Bakrac's asking of leading questions of the witness. My -- I have a submission on this, an objection to the asking of leading questions and a brief submission in relation to that. But before I make that submission, I'd like to know in fact whether Mr. Bakrac was able to meet with the witness before his testimony.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Bakrac, there's a question -- well, first of all, leading questions, of course, Mr. Bakrac is cross-examining the witness in which leading questions as such are not prohibited.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: That's exactly the matter I wanted to raise, Your Honour. I wanted to object to Mr. Bakrac cross-examining a witness who is a witness in his favour if he is in possession of information --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So you would say that Mr. Bakrac is not only eliciting answers on the subject matter of the examination-in-chief or on matters of credibility and reliability but he is also questioning the witness under Rule 90(H) - what is it? - small (ii), I think, that is, eliciting evidence from the witness which supports that party's case. Is that ...

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: That's right, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And there you would expect Mr. Bakrac to refrain from leading questions.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Correct, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Bakrac, the questions you have put to the witness when did you put leading questions to him, was that in any way related to the examination-in-chief; or were you eliciting evidence under Rule - and let me be very precise - Rule 90(H)(i), last part, where it reads: "The witness is able to give evidence relevant to the case for the cross-examining party to subject matter of that case." Were you eliciting that kind of evidence or were you challenging the evidence which was led in-chief?

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I was not challenging the credibility of the witness. My question was more pursuant to 90(H), as you said. And I can respond to what my learned friend said. I did have an occasion to meet with the witness for ten minutes. I did not make any notes. I didn't have a pen or paper in front of me. We discussed matters in general. I never showed the witness these two documents. We didn't discuss them. And this is something that the witness can confirm.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And that was before the witness started giving his evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, of course, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think, in view of your answer, that the appropriate way of questioning the witness would be not to put leading questions to him. Is that, Ms. Marcus ...

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Would you please keep that in mind. You may proceed, Mr. Bakrac.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. Please bear with me for a moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Witness, one minute and one question more.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we go back to page 1.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Can you look at the third bullet point, please, which reads: "He continued maintaining contact with members of the Army of Yugoslavia." As part of your operative work, did you monitor individuals who had some dealings with or were in any way associated with the security of the Army of Yugoslavia?

utterances.speaker: DST-063 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not in that line of work. That was not part of our duty. But if -- we would come across them as part of some other work.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: In that case, would you also report to the military security structure, or did it remain strictly within the authority of the MUP?

utterances.speaker: DST-063 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I can't tell you exactly. I think it was treated as internal information.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Thank you very much, witness, for the answers you gave me.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And, Your Honours, for the time assigned to me. I have completed my examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Bakrac. Ms. Marcus, are you ready to cross-examine the witness?

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You will now be cross-examined by Ms. Marcus. Ms. Marcus is counsel for the Prosecution. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Good morning, DST-063.

utterances.speaker: DST-063 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: During your testimony last week, you were asked whether the Vojvodina SUP and the Serbian MUP had a joint or a separate chain of command. You stated, at transcript page 13562: "... I think that at some crucial moments, they had a joint chain of command, absolutely. A Joint Command function." Early 1992, they had a joint command. Can you explain what you meant by "joint command"?

utterances.speaker: DST-063 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, if I cast my mind back to that, an event which would have trigged our joint work, well, I wouldn't refer it -- refer to it as "command." Rather, it would have been joint co-operation. Command would sound like we were in the army, and we didn't have that sort of work.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: This co-operation you refer to existed prior to 1992 as well, didn't it?

utterances.speaker: DST-063 [Resumed]
utterances.text: But, of course. But it was with all the services of all the republics, and not just Serbia. We were a separate service only formally at the level of the province of Vojvodina. But that was formally only.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Now, with respect to the DB, the state security, isn't it true that prior to 1992 the federal DB governed this co-ordination, direction, and reconciling of the works of the SDBs throughout the provinces and the republics?

utterances.speaker: DST-063 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. As far as I know, that's true. They treated on equal terms all the provinces and republics.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Now, during your testimony at page 13559, you were describing your only chain of reporting as a DB operative. This was when you were an operative in the Vojvodina DB in 1990. You stated that your superior "was the chief of the group, working on counter-intelligence activities, and he was" - pardon my pronunciation - "he was Stevan Pecelj. "He answered to the chief of the department, Djordje Gojkovic, of that section." Then you said that Gojkovic's superior "was the chief of the provincial State Security Service. At that time, it was Ratko Sikimic." You then go on to stay that Sikimic was responsible to the chief of the federal service. Now my question to you is: Therefore, according to your evidence, if we understood you correctly, the reporting line from the Vojvodina DB went straight up to the federal DB in 1990; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DST-063 [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, both to -- up to the federal and the republican DB. And I mean the DB of Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: And that was the case in 1991 as well?

utterances.speaker: DST-063 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am referring to 1991, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Now, during your testimony last week when you were asked about the changes in the work of the Vojvodina SUP after the multi-party elections, you replied that the situation: "Required a greater effort on our part, in terms of taking in the overall security situation." Can you explain what you meant by that?

utterances.speaker: DST-063 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, what I said the last time, I believe, was that the elections had taken place in the various republics and that the assessment made at the time was that there was an extremely aggressive, and, at times, very hostile attitude coming from the Republic of Croatia. Since my centre has under its purview territory which borders with the Republic of Croatia along the length of some 130 and 140 kilometres, and since in my territory we had a sizeable Croat population, the situation required the service to invest more efforts in collecting information with a view to averting a conflict in that area.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Now, at page 13586, you were asked what territory you were trying to protect by gathering this information that you just described. Your answer was: "The territory of the Republic of Serbia." So is it your evidence that matters of overall security are those which would impact upon the territory of Serbia as a whole?

utterances.speaker: DST-063 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would first like to say that the term "defence" is something that does not stand, in my view, here. Having control over the territory bordering Republic of Croatia for the purpose of preventing possible problems that could occur in our territory; that's what it implied.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Okay. Well, perhaps there was something I said which was maybe misconstrued. But I was asking specifically about your information-gathering activities. And you said that you had to put a greater effort in to take in the overall security situation. So my question to you was: These matters that affected the overall security are, in fact, matters that affect the entirety of the Republic of Serbia; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: DST-063 [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the time, no. I'm talking about late 1990 and early 1991. That was regular procedure, part of our service's work, making assessments of possible problems. What we did was we had operatives focussing more on that specific territory.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Okay. I understand. And what about after May of 1991?

utterances.speaker: DST-063 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Now that you've mentioned the date, and it was a date that made the overall situation much more complex, but this time I'm talking about the area of Croatia, the area of Vukovar, yes, it required additional involvement of operatives, and that was the period when my involvement started. Until that point, I was not involved.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: And the matters relating to security at that time impacted on the Republic of Serbia as a whole, not just on Vojvodina; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: DST-063 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: And these matters would be the kind of matters which would require sending of information up to the hierarchy at the highest levels, because they are matters which affected the overall security; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: DST-063 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. But I cannot confirm to which level all this went. I was just an operative. You must understand that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Marcus, your question in relation to the highest levels in the hierarchy does not specify what hierarchy and what highest levels, which makes the answer, at least, ambiguous.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: DST-063, I was specifically referring to this information about the overall security and its path up to the leadership of the Serbian DB. Does that change your answer at all?

utterances.speaker: DST-063 [Resumed]
utterances.text: At my level, or, rather, my understanding of who was informed went up to the chief of my centre. I -- and my colleagues would brief him either in writing or orally. Everything else was outside of my scope. It was in -- in part of his duties. He would choose whom to forward it to.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: So if I understand you correctly, it was the chief of the centre - I suppose you mean the Novi Sad centre - who had the authority to determine how far the information would be sent or to whom; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DST-063 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, you understood me well.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Now, if there were information that -- that you felt, as an operative, would have to be sent up to the leadership of the Serbian DB, and if the head of the Novi Sad DB decided not to, what would be the consequences?

utterances.speaker: DST-063 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the chief would decide, and things would be that way. There would be no consequences, of course.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Were you always informed of where your information -- what path your information took after you provided it? Were you informed of where your reports ended up?

utterances.speaker: DST-063 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I wasn't told about it. The practice wasn't that we get told.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Now, on page 5, your entry, in relation to D205, which you say is a report by you, your entry -- this -- this report also contains information relating to combat activities, including your assessment of the combat readiness of the Army of the RSK. Your comment on this document is that: "I obtained this information by talking to people in Eastern Slavonia. This does not mean that this information is absolutely correct." Now, my question to you is: I was not able to see anywhere in the report where you state that the information may not be correct. How did you distinguish in your reports between reports which were correct and reports which were not correct?

utterances.speaker: DST-063 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is difficult to pronounce any report as fully correct on the face of it. That's why there was a practice in place where every document would be double-checked repeatedly. This also included looking into the reliability of the source. In other words, a report would be written and -- well, now I can't recall. But based on the information it contains, this specific report, I think it definitely merited the attention.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: I'm not sure I understood your last comment. You said: "... a report would be written -- well, now I can't recall. But based on the information it contains, this specific report, I think it definitely merited the attention." My question to you had been: How would the reader of this report know that the information may not be correct if you didn't say so in that report? That really was my question.

utterances.speaker: DST-063 [Resumed]
utterances.text: A reader would review the contents of the document and would then get back to me and tell me what needed doing in order to verify the information contained therein. I said that the information was supposed to be double-checked. But what sort of information returned, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, you have given evidence about a meeting attended by Zoran Janackovic, Goran Hadzic, Ratko Sikimic, Ilija Kojic, and others from the JNA and SDB and SSDB. Aside from Mr. Janackovic, what other members of the Serbian DB were present at that meeting?

utterances.speaker: DST-063 [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I can remember, he was the only one.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Who was it who called the meeting?

utterances.speaker: DST-063 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know who proposed for the meeting to be held. My chief told me to appear there at a specified date and time.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Your chief being Ratko Sikimic?

utterances.speaker: DST-063 [Resumed]
utterances.text: My immediate supervisor was Djordje Gojkovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Apart from those you listed in your testimony who attended the meeting, do you recall anyone else who attended?

utterances.speaker: DST-063 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, in addition to four of us that I named, there may have been up to ten people in total. No, I don't think I missed anyone.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: You testified that according to what was discussed and assigned at the meeting, the intelligence-gathering process was to be changed. And this gathering of security information from Croatia was primarily due to the hostilities in that area. Would that be accurate?

utterances.speaker: DST-063 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't understand. The result of the information and hostile activities. I don't understand that part.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Let me take it step by step. How would the intelligence-gathering process be changed according to what was discussed and assigned during that meeting?

utterances.speaker: DST-063 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It would be changed in such a way that the presence of operatives in the areas in question was possible. In other words, there was possibility of direct insight into the situation. Up until that point, all intelligence was based on information received from citizens fleeing Croatia and coming to Serbia. The change in the situation was in the fact that I could cross the border.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Now, these security concerns would implicate potential security risks not only for the Vojvodina area but for the entirety of Serbia. Wouldn't that be correct?

utterances.speaker: DST-063 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Now, during your testimony last week, at page 13571 and 2, you were asked what happened at the meeting. You said that: "On behalf of the State Security Service, actually, the position of the State Security Service was that I should go there and the colleague of mine from Novi Sad, Radovan Vucurevic. And from the public security service, Momcilo Radovic, aka Pujo, and Boro Predragovic." So you your colleague Vucurevic were the ones to be dispatched from the State Security Service; is that right?

utterances.speaker: DST-063 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: What was it, to your knowledge, that led the Serbian DB to select you and Vucurevic for this particular mission?

utterances.speaker: DST-063 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would link it up with an event that took place one or two days before the meeting. As part of our regular duties, Mr. Vucurevic and myself were escorting a member of the SFRY Presidency, Mr. Branko Kostic, to a meeting in Borovo Selo. If I'm not mistaken, it was on the 27th of July, 1991. My task, as well as Vucurevic's, was to take the state's delegation across the Danube river to secure them during their visit and bring them back to the territory of Vojvodina or Serbia safely. I can only assume that this was then just a continuation of my crossings of the border.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Jordash.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: I do think there is a possibility of the Court being mislead, that there is a hidden question or hidden premise in my learned friend's previous question which has not been either noticed by the witness or certainly hasn't been addressed, which is the -- the premise being that the state security of Serbia sent the witness. The witness hasn't said that. I don't think his previous testimony said that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think, as a matter of fact, that is not a kind of comments -- of course you can raise this matter, but the witness now is aware of everything you mention. And I think that it should have been done in the absence of the witness or the witness having taken his earphones off.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Well, if that's Your Honours' ruling, then, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Ms. Marcus, you've heard the comment which, again, appropriately should have been made in the absence of the witness or with the witness taking his earphones off. But if you want to further pursue this specific aspect, you're invited to do so.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. I didn't realize there was any confusion on this issue.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: DST-063, who did you view was deploying you to Croatia, to the areas that you were deployed to, as a -- as a DB operative? Who was it -- under whose authority were you being deployed?

utterances.speaker: DST-063 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Me and my colleague were selected by my chief, Djordje Gojkovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: But the ultimate mission and -- which was the result of the tasks assigned at that meeting was a federal DB/Serbian DB mission; isn't that correct? Thus, the presence of the highest level DB officials.

utterances.speaker: DST-063 [Resumed]
utterances.text: On one hand, yes. But I believe the republican state security and the federal state security were interested in gaining insight of the situation in the area of question. We're talking about 1991, when this was all one state.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Now, you stated during your testimony last week at 13573 that your mission was to: "... obtain data and information such as could indicate that a part of these interethnic conflicts would be, could be, spilled over to also the territories of Vojvodina and Serbia." Now, you were -- were you in a position to have refused this mission? Basically, my question is: Did you, on the ground, in the Novi Sad DB, have the authority to say to those in the federal DB at that meeting, "No, I'm sorry, we cannot carry this out"?

utterances.speaker: DST-063 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't see any purpose in refusing to do that. And, secondly, we are professionals. There was no reason for us to refuse it. I don't believe anyone would have.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That is not an answer to the question. You said, as a matter of fact you had no reason to refuse it. The question was: If you would have had reasons, would you have been in a position to refuse this assignment and this deployment?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I was in a position to refuse such a deployment, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Would the Novi Sad DB have been in a position to refuse a deployment? I'm just trying to clarify. You individually, personally, may have refused, but would your authorities have been in a position to refuse the assignment?

utterances.speaker: DST-063 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I cannot give you a comment on that. I don't know what my chief or Chief Sikimic could have or should have done. I don't want to engage in any guess-work here.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: DST-063, do we understand correctly that this mission was one which lasted, for you, from the moment of that meeting in July 1991 all the way through to the Erdut Agreement in 1995?

utterances.speaker: DST-063 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I was going to the area throughout that period, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: During that time, were you deployed to any other regions, apart from the area of Eastern Slavonia?

utterances.speaker: DST-063 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: During your testimony last week at page 13592, when you were asked about a document relating to events in Dalj on the 21st of September, 1991, you stated that at this time you were in Borovo Selo and you probably went to Dalj. "I cannot dispute that," you said. Do you recall saying that?

utterances.speaker: DST-063 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I suppose I did say so.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: So on and after the 21st of September, 1991, you were in Dalj gathering information as a DB operative; is that right?

utterances.speaker: DST-063 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Were you also in Dalj gathering information on or about the 4th of October of 1991?

utterances.speaker: DST-063 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I probably was.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: There has been evidence in this case that in September and October of 1991 Serb forces, particularly SAO SBWS TO and SAO SBWS MUP forces, arrested Croat civilians and kept them in a detention facility in the police building in Dalj. On the 21st of September, 1991, Goran Hadzic and Zeljko Raznjatovic, aka Arkan, visited the detention facility and ordered the release of two of the detainees. According to the evidence, Serb forces, in particular the SBWS TO and MUP forces, and Arkan's SDG shot and killed 11 detainees and buried them in a mass grave in the village of Celije. You told us that you did not find out about this incident until at least 1993 when you heard it from Cizmic. Are you saying that in spite of being in Dalj and in the area of Dalj during and after the 21st of September, 1991, that you never heard of the detention and execution of ethnic Croat civilians in the Dalj Police Station?

utterances.speaker: DST-063 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's precisely what I'm saying. And if you want me to, I can explain.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Please do.

utterances.speaker: DST-063 [Resumed]
utterances.text: First, the incident in itself is horrific. Being there, under those circumstances, in an area of combat activity, I don't think I'd be able to find a person who would have the courage to report it. And I'm talking about 1993. The situation settle the down. The local authorities became operational. I met Cizmic. I think he was the commander of the Dalj Police Station at the time. That was different. Whereas, this particular incident was in 1991. Everything was possible. Anything could happen anywhere. And it did. Had I known of this incident, I would have included it in my report, without going into what should happen beyond that. But I would have stated it as information, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: A witness who testified recently told this Chamber that everybody in Dalj knew about this incident at that time. In particular, those in the police.

utterances.speaker: DST-063 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe him.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: How is it that you are the only police officer who was there who didn't hear about this incident?

utterances.speaker: DST-063 [Resumed]
utterances.text: First of all, I don't know even that there was a Dalj Police Station in 1991. I'm not sure. Well, as for all the policemen being aware of it, that's something that I can accept as his statement, a generalisation. I myself did not go into -- to Dalj to investigate. I had a mission, and I was supposed to check something in respect of an individual that I was supposed to identify. Perhaps they had a kind of deference for me from the police service there, so they didn't approach me on this. But I'm speculating now.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Why would they have had a kind of deference for you?

utterances.speaker: DST-063 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, how would I know that?

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: There has been evidence in this case that on the 4th of October, 1991, Serb forces, including Arkan's SDG, and members of the SAO SBWS TO and MUP returned to the police building in Dalj and shot 26 ethnic Croat civilians who were detained there. The bodies, according to the evidence, were then dumped into the Danube river. You testified that you were in Dalj on or about the 4th of October, 1991. In your comment chart, D388, MFI, on page 1, you commented on Exhibit P11, which is a report on this incident. You stated that you heard about these events considerably later. Do you recall how you heard about these events?

utterances.speaker: DST-063 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can I make a correction? I cannot state with any certainty that I was in Dalj on the 4th of October. It was a period of time when I made trips there. But it's difficult for me, 20 years on, to know where I was on a specific date. Now let me answer your question. After I got to know Zeljko Cizmic, I suppose we were reminiscing about the events from the -- these war-torn areas. He may have brought it up and told me the story. But that's where this story between us ended as well.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: But that was a couple of years later; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DST-063 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, after this incident, yes, I suppose that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: So in spite of being in or, as you've now clarified, near Dalj at this time, you did not hear anything about the execution of 26 ethnic Croat civilians in the Dalj Police Station on the 4th of October, 1991, at that time?

utterances.speaker: DST-063 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Now, really, I can't be as precise about the dates, and this is a very precise date. So, simply ...

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Now, earlier you tried to explain to us that if Arkan had -- and his forces had attacked civilians, if there were potentially to be serious security consequences of that attack, it would then have been the kind of information that would have been of importance to you in your work. So is this an instance where the assessment would have been that there were no serious consequences of this kind of a killing? Why would this particular instance not have come to your attention, not have been something that would you have come across in your work?

utterances.speaker: DST-063 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Such an incident would definitely merit our attention. But let me underline the fact that we are talking about 1991, a period of intense combat activities. What followed beyond 1991 was a period of peace and stabilisation in the area. There is an enormous difference between what the situation was like in 1991 and the subsequent years.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: And in this particular instance, you did not see or learn about the bodies of these ethnic Croatian victims floating down the Danube from Dalj.

utterances.speaker: DST-063 [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I remember, I did not. And I most certainly did not see.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Did you ever hear of the SAO SBWS TO committing crimes alongside Arkan and his men in 1991?

utterances.speaker: DST-063 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: What about the SBWS MUP? Did you ever hear about MUP members committing crimes, along with Arkan's SDG and the TO, in 1991?

utterances.speaker: DST-063 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: There has been evidence in this case that in 1991 the SNB was also participating in crimes in co-operation with Arkan, the TO, and other Serb forces in the region. Did you learn of any co-operation between the SNB and Arkan and his SDG to commit crimes in the region?

utterances.speaker: DST-063 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: There has been evidence in this case that on the 9th of November, 1991, Arkan led the SDG and the SBWS TO and MUP in arresting at least nine ethnic Hungarians and Croat civilians and took them to the Erdut training centre. They shot and killed these civilians the next day, according to the evidence. Did you know anything about this incident at the time?

utterances.speaker: DST-063 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: So I suppose you also don't know anything about several days after this when members of the SNB of the SBWS, in co-operation with the SDG, arrested and killed some relatives of the original victims and threw their bodies into a well in Borovo. Have you heard of that incident?

utterances.speaker: DST-063 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: There's also been evidence that on the 11th of November, 1991, the SDG, SBWS TO and MUP forces arrested seven non-Serb civilians and detained them in a house in Erdut. They beat and interrogated them in that house, according to the evidence. That night, Arkan's Men took them to the training centre in Erdut. There, they killed the five civilians. Did you learn about these killings?

utterances.speaker: DST-063 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Now, DST-063, from your answers to these questions, it is clear that for the killings that the Prosecution has charged in the SBWS region, you did not even learn that a crime had been committed during the time that you were an operative in Eastern Slavonia in 1991. You only found out about these murders long after they had been committed. Would you agree that you are not able to provide accurate information on the Serb forces who were involved in crimes in Eastern Slavonia during that time?

utterances.speaker: DST-063 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can confirm that you understood me well. You enumerated several cases that I'm hearing of for the first time here and now. If I may add: November was a period of intense combat activities and operations around the city of Vukovar, and my activities at the time were minimal. And I'm not even sure whether I was physically present there at the time.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: So you confirm that you do not have information about the Serb forces and their activities and involvement in crimes in Eastern Slavonia in 1991; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DST-063 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I confirm that.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: The Defence informed us that you have knowledge of the appearance of Arkan in the region, Arkan's training camp, and Arkan's relationship with Badza. Did you tell the Defence that can you provide information about Arkan's arrival in the region, his Erdut training camp, and his relationship with Badza?

utterances.speaker: DST-063 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I don't know how this came about.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Jordash.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Again --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You would like to have it literally quoted?

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Well, yes -- the summary says the witness will -- [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Well, let's -- let's -- Ms. Marcus, there apparently is a comment on the way in which you put it to the witness. Would you please literally use the words the Defence has used.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Would the Court Officer please call up Exhibit D31.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: DST-063, what you will see on the screen in front of you is a military security report regarding the SDB's training centre in Erdut, which is dated 19 October 1991. On page 1, it states that a certain Lieutenant Blagojevic had contacted Arkan at the Erdut centre, and Arkan had told him that: "Weaponry, ammunition, and mines and explosives had been supplied by the MUP and the Ministry of Defence of the Republic of Serbia and that he had been distributing them to the TO staffs in Erdut, Sarvas, and Borovo Selo ..." Did you know that these ministries of the Republic of Serbia were involved with Arkan's training centre?

utterances.speaker: DST-063 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Absolutely not.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Could the Court Officer now please call up P1078.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: This is another military security report regarding Arkan and the SDG, dated January 1992.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Could I please have page 3 in the English and page 2 in the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: This report lists the vehicles and weapons that Arkan has at the Erdut centre. The report goes on to state that these weapons and vehicles were acquired from the TO, MUP, and JNA. Then on page 4 in the English, it states that Arkan is: "... openly supported by the MUP, TO, and MNO of the Republic of Serbia." And that he is officially subordinated to the JNA, but this is only formal. And he enters and leaves the combat area as he pleases. Do you know where Arkan got the authority to come and go as he pleases, without being reprimanded by any of the authorities?

utterances.speaker: DST-063 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. This report was provided by a military man who had such information. I'm not saying it is correct, but that person was in a situation where he could obtain this type of information, number of vehicles, and so on. I could not.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Isn't it possible that had you gathered information, you would have learned, yourself, about Arkan's relationship with the Serbian MUP and DB?

utterances.speaker: DST-063 [Resumed]
utterances.text: How could I have gathered such information? Who was I supposed to ask? You must understand that I was an operative, and that is the lowest level within my service at the time.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Thank you. I'm done with the document. DST-063, I understand from your testimony last week that the 1st of August, 1991, was the date of your first trip into Croatia following the meeting in July. Is that accurate?

utterances.speaker: DST-063 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: You testified that on that day you went to Borovo Selo and met

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: between March 1991 and August 1991. Is that your evidence?

utterances.speaker: DST-063 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot say that it was on the 31st of March, that that was the start date. But after the events in Borovo Selo, they did organise on their own, yes.

utterances.speaker: DST-063 [Resumed]
utterances.text: inform you of his Serbian DB affiliation?

utterances.speaker: DST-063 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I hear this for the first time. The only contact was through me, as far as I know.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Your Honours, this might be a good time for our break, if you're --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you give us an indication as to how much time would you need after the break.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: I will certainly use the entirety of the next session, with your leave. I'll do my best to finish by the end of the day.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That would be appreciated. We'll take a break. And we resume at 12.30.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Marcus, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. I just wanted to mention that we have a submission we'd like to make in relation to the next witness and the circumstances. If possible, we'd like to make it before the end of today. I think that would be useful.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And how much time would that take?

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Maybe about ten minutes or so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ten minutes. I will give you ten minutes at the end of this session.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: DST-063, did you tell the Defence before your testimony that it

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: get in touch with? Did you inform them of that before your testimony?

utterances.speaker: DST-063 [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I recall, I -- no, they did not. I did not.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Could I have D398 on the screen, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: The document we're about to look at is one which you commented in your comments chart and page 7, and you testified about this last week at pages 13603 to 4. You confirmed that this report was prepared by you. The front page is apparently a cover page forwarding your report to Jovica Stanisic personally at the Serbian DB, which, you say, was done on your suggestion. This report details an incident on the 16th of February, 1993, when the RSK army surrounded the RSK MUP building in Vukovar in an attempt to forcibly remove some of the RSK MUP leadership. Do you recall this incident?

utterances.speaker: DST-063 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Could I please have page 3 in B/C/S and page 2 in English. Focussing, please, on the bottom of page 3 in B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Now, on this page it states that the demand was for Ilija Kojic, who was Assistant Minister of the RSK MUP, to be replaced, in addition to

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: replaced, and he was accused - pardon me - he was accused of allegedly cooperating with the RDB of the MUP of Serbia. To your knowledge, why was there a demand for Ilija Kojic to be replaced?

utterances.speaker: DST-063 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Where co-operation with the DB and the MUP of Serbia is referred to, what is meant there is my -- is my contacts with him. I don't know of any other co-operation with the MUP. As for the demands, that's not something I can speculate about.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Perhaps there might be some misunderstanding. My question was that in this document it states that

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: MUP of Serbia. And then my question to you, which I think you've answered now, was that there was a -- why -- do you know why there was a demand for Ilija Kojic to be replaced. Now, you've told us that you -- you do not know. So certainly by the time you prepared this report you were aware

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: for the Serbian DB in 1991; is that accurate?

utterances.speaker: DST-063 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I'm not aware of it.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Now, I asked you a few questions ago, How do you know that he didn't work for the DB. You told us that this is what you know. How did you know that he never worked for the Serbian DB?

utterances.speaker: DST-063 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I can't be positive about it, but I suppose the man would have told me so.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Could the Court Officer please call up P407, on which the witness provided comments in his comments chart on page 4.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: was working in counter-intelligence in the Novi Sad SDB in 1991. That's at page 13587. Now, this report, as can you see, is dated the 22nd of February, 1993, and it's an update on the same incident. The first paragraph of the report discusses a conflict between Ilija Kojic and what is described as the head of the "non-existent Vukovar TO," Miroljub Vukovic. Can you assist us in understanding what is meant by "non-existent Vukovar TO"?

utterances.speaker: DST-063 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot confirm all the statements made during in that period of time, but I do know for a fact that Milorad Vujovic [as interpreted] had been a commander of the Vukovar TO for a while. Why it is referred to

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Okay. Now, the report states that the information has gotten out of control and turned against Ilija Kojic, Slobodan Ivkovic, Lazic, and Kostic. The source of this information suggests that Kojic staged the conflict in order to effect a change of leadership of Vukovar TO. The second paragraph reads: "The source said Serbia was to blame for all these developments, that is, the assistant minister of the Ministry of the Interior of Serbia, Jovica Stanisic, who tried to use Ivkovic, Kojic, and Kostic and others to turn the Krajina into a twilight zone." Can you explain, if you know, what was meant by Stanisic trying to "use Ivkovic, Kojic, Kostic and others to turn Krajina into a twilight zone"?

utterances.speaker: DST-063 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't know what the author of the text or the source of information meant. It is a subjective view, after all. But I can't see how it was possible for anyone at all to change anything significantly in the region, apart from a political solution. That's my view. It is up to the source of information to provide explanations for his statements.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Lazic and Kostic are mentioned in this report, which follows up on the incident that you reported about just a few days previously. But your report did not mention either Lazic or Kostic.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: interpretation of the events by Vodolija.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: What did you know about Ivkovic and Lazic's connections to Jovica Stanisic at the time of these reports?

utterances.speaker: DST-063 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Absolutely nothing.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Do you have any reason to disbelieve whether Stanisic would have done something to encourage conflict?

utterances.speaker: DST-063 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot comment on it. I can give you a general statement. I don't see that anything significant could change over there. And who would have wanted to have a "twilight zone" over there? The area was inhabited. There were people living there. And nobody could permit themselves to lead them into such a situation. And who would have dared to? Individuals mattered least under those circumstances.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: There is nothing which would cause you to doubt the source's assertion about Mr. Stanisic's relationship with Ivkovic, Kojic, and Kostic, is there?

utterances.speaker: DST-063 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have no doubts. With a high degree of certainty, I can say that the individuals mentioned here never, ever saw Mr. Stanisic. Had they seen him, they would have boasted about it. Mr. Stanisic was the leader of my service. To me, this sounds incredible.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: I'm finished with the document. Thank you. Now, you testified last week that you had never seen or met Boro and Pujo until the meeting that you all attended with Janackovic; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DST-063 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I had never seen Boro, but I knew Bojo [as interpreted] through various sports activities. I wasn't familiar with his professional dealings.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: And after you were dispatched along with Boro and Pujo and Vucurevic to Vukovar, you testified that did you not know what activities they conducted; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DST-063 [Resumed]
utterances.text: In principle, yes. I know that they toured the newly established police stations, that's all.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: So I take it you didn't know that Boro and Pujo were involved in meetings of the SBWS TO along with Ilija Kojic and Dragan Lazic; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Sorry, can I object to the way that's phrased. Is that the Prosecution's case? Does that arise from evidence? It's presented as fact, but we don't know the basis for that.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I'll clarify.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please to do.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Yes, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: That has been evidence in this case that Boro and Pujo were involved in meetings in the SBWS TO, along with Ilija Kojic and Dragan Lazic. Are you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: DST-063 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: There has also been evidence in this case that Boro and Pujo were involved with the Serbian DB in 1991 during the same time that you were in Eastern Slavonia. Did you know anything about this?

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Sorry. Could I --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
