utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: DST-063, would you agree that in 1991, during the time that the security situation in Serbia was getting more complex, there was something of a reorganisation of police forces, and special police units, or PJM detachments, were formed. Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: DST-063 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know about that, the special police and reorganisation.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Are you aware of the instruction by the minister of the interior to form PJM detachments?

utterances.speaker: DST-063 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: So you're not aware of a PJM detachment in Novi Sad under the command of Obrad Stevanovic; is that your evidence?

utterances.speaker: DST-063 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I am aware of that. But I don't know when the minister took the decision to establish the PJMs. I am aware of it, but only of it existing at a later date.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: According to your knowledge, from what time are you aware of the PJM detachment in Novi Sad under the command of Obrad Stevanovic?

utterances.speaker: DST-063 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot specify when, but it was 1992 or 1993. That was when I became aware of this term "PJM." Unfortunately, I cannot help you beyond that. And I'm hearing for the first time that Mr. Stevanovic was the commander of the PJM in Novi Sad.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: According to the information we have, Obrad Stevanovic was the commander of the PJM overall. But the commander of the PJM in Novi Sad was Boro Predragovic. Were you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: DST-063 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That, yes. But Obrad Stevanovic was not the commander of the PJM in Novi Sad, as you told me a moment ago.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: According to your knowledge, was Obrad Stevanovic the overall commander of the PJM in the region?

utterances.speaker: DST-063 [Resumed]
utterances.text: In what region? I apologise.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: In the broader region surrounding Novi Sad, in the Vojvodina area.

utterances.speaker: DST-063 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is possible, but I was not aware of it. And I'm not aware of it now.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: From what date are you aware of Boro Predragovic being the commander of the PJM in Novi Sad?

utterances.speaker: DST-063 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was certainly later than 1991, but I cannot tell you anything more precise than that.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Were you aware of Dragoslav Krsmanovic being Boro Predragovic's deputy?

utterances.speaker: DST-063 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Now, at the time the security situation was worsening, namely in May 1991, the Serbian minister of the interior adopted a decision on Operative Action Danube. Are you familiar with Operative Action Danube?

utterances.speaker: DST-063 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: So you will be able to confirm for us that under Operative Action Danube operative staff monitored the territory along the border with the Republic of Croatia; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DST-063 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: And the staff of Operative Action Danube were situated in Novi Sad; is that right?

utterances.speaker: DST-063 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That I do not know. I'm not even sure we're talking about the same action, because my service was forwarding its report as a part of this operative action. Now, what the public security service was doing, I would not want to speculate on that.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: So you confirm that your operative work was, in fact, a part of Operative Action Danube.

utterances.speaker: DST-063 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Did you mention this to the Defence before you came to testify here?

utterances.speaker: DST-063 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Now, correct me if I'm wrong: As far as I know, the territory covered by this Operative Action Danube was divided into three parts; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DST-063 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That I don't know. You reminded me of the action. I wouldn't have remembered its name on my own without your help.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Based on your evidence, you carried out your functions within the Novi Sad DB in Bac municipality; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DST-063 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not only in the municipality of Bac. The municipalities bordering with Croatia are Bac, Backa Palanka, and Beocin.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: So who was the commander within Operative Action Danube to whom you were responsible?

utterances.speaker: DST-063 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That I don't know. My reports that were part of this action were drafted by me and sent to the centre, which does not necessarily mean that such reports, if the contents merited it, were forwarded to the centre down there. But who was leading the action, that I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Would you agree with me that Miodrag Zavisic was the commander of Operative Action Danube in the area of Bac municipality?

utterances.speaker: DST-063 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot agree with you because I don't know. He was there, but what his position was, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Can you explain to us how is it possible to be an operative within an operative action and not know who's the commander of the operative action in which you're working?

utterances.speaker: DST-063 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can explain it in quite simple terms. First of all, we have two different services involved here. My level of awareness at the time is very modest. And the name of the commander of the Operative Action Danube was not something that would mean anything to me then or now. I had very clear tasks, and I just list them as being related to the Operative Action Danube, and that's all.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Could I have one moment, please, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: DST-063, I'm going to ask you about something you said earlier. I'm just looking for the transcript reference. It was today. Now, on page 36 of the temporary transcript, I asked you: "Do we understand correctly that this mission was one which lasted, for you, from the moment of that meeting in July 1991 all the way through to the Erdut Agreement in 1995?" Your response was: "Yes. I was going to the area throughout that period, yes." Then you were asked: "During that time, were you deployed to any other regions, apart from the area of Eastern Slavonia?" Your answer was: "No." That's the end of the quote. Can you confirm for us that you did not take part in any other operative tasks anywhere else other than Slavonia and the Vojvodina area in 1991?

utterances.speaker: DST-063 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can absolutely confirm that, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Have you ever seen your DB personnel file?

utterances.speaker: DST-063 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I may have, but I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Well, let's take a look at your personnel file. Your official record does not seem to correspond to what you were actually doing.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Understood, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Now, DST-063, are you aware that Jovica Stanisic also had Milan Radonjic retroactively officially deployed to Kosovo from May to November of 1991?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the counsel please repeat the name of the person.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Thank you. It was Milan Radonjic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Are you aware that Jovica Stanisic also had Dragan Filipovic retroactively officially deployed to Kosovo from April to November 1991?

utterances.speaker: DST-063 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Are you aware that Jovica Stanisic also had Franko Simatovic retroactively officially deployed to Kosovo from April to November 1991?

utterances.speaker: DST-063 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Were you operating in co-ordination or co-operation with Franko Simatovic in Eastern Slavonia in 1991?

utterances.speaker: DST-063 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. And I've never seen him there.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: So your evidence would be that all of these retroactive assignments to Kosovo would have been for the purpose of justification of financial expenses incurred in SBWS. Is that your evidence?

utterances.speaker: DST-063 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can only speak for myself. And roughly, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Could I ask you: You say, I can't speak for the others. To what extent can you confirm that it was the financial aspects that caused your retroactive deployment in Kosovo?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I cannot be absolutely certain about it. I can see that as the only possible reason, because I do know that there was a problem of that nature.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: How did you know that; and what was exactly that problem?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I know that I was supposed to get some finances that would cover per diems and separated life and that there was no modus that could be found to take care of it. And I do remember that it took a while before it was resolved, if it was resolved at all. That's all I can say.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Did you receive those per diems?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think so, but after quite a delay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. You're talking about the delay. Is it true that you did receive them, although delayed; or do you say, It was delayed but whether I received it finally, yes or no, I do not remember? Which of the two?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think I did receive it. I'm convinced I received it. But I cannot remember when or any details about it. But I do believe that it was resolved positively for me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Ms. Marcus. I was asking the question because initially the witness said that he -- he could only assume a certain explanation, where there seems to be at least some factual ground for it. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Last clarification I have on this particular issue. So are you saying that this financial payment that you received, that you ultimately received, per diems, reimbursement for expenses, et cetera, which you say was justified by this false deployment document, that you received that from the Serbian DB in recognition of a work that you did in the SBWS in 1991?

utterances.speaker: DST-063 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wouldn't describe it as some kind of recognition for my work. I believe it was something that I was due anyhow, and there was no other way of resolving it. I just cannot see what other intention may have been behind a decision such as this. What would be the intention of it? What would be the purpose of it?

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: So, in your view, due to your work in SBWS in 1991 for the Serbian DB, you were due this money as compensation, reimbursement for expenses, et cetera. Do I have that right?

utterances.speaker: DST-063 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It was due to me, but there was also the administrative problem of the close proximity of that region. Very often I would return to Novi Sad, and simply a mode was found. I could have been deployed to the Nis centre, which is about 300 kilometres away from Novi Sad, and I would get the same.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: So you were being paid as if you were carrying out operations or operative actions in Kosovo, although you were actually carrying out your operative actions in SBWS; is that right?

utterances.speaker: DST-063 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I think now you've come closest to the truth.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Your Honours, I have, I would say, about a half an hour to 40 minutes more of cross-examination, and I'm conscious of the decisions that we have to make about the next witness. I just wanted to raise that for Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. We'll -- Witness DST-063, we would need a bit more of your time tomorrow. And we'd like to see you back tomorrow in the afternoon. I again instruct you that you should not speak with anyone about your testimony, whether already given or still to be given tomorrow, and I'd like to invite you to follow the usher and leave the courtroom. See you back tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, now everything -- [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Let me just verify that.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: This morning before court I sent around electronic versions of this submission and another one that I was going to make, so I'm sorry that that didn't reach -- seems not to have reached the booths. We're going to send one through right now. I don't know which booth is going to get the hard copy. If someone tells us, tells the Case Manager, which person to send it to by e-mail, we will do that immediately.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Sorry, were they sent to the Defence? We haven't found them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, but I do understand it's for the purposes of -- we usually, Mr. Jordash, also do not send to the parties already a copy of what are read-like statements or these kind of things. It's purely in order to facilitate the interpreters to do their job. Nothing else. Please proceed, Ms. Marcus, if you would, at least when you read, do it slowly.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: I will do so, Your Honours. The Prosecution submission is that we have been detrimentally prejudiced in the context of our preparations for the testimony of DST-040. For the reasons I'm going to set forth, the Prosecution requests that cross-examination be postponed until after the adjournment. The Defence informed the Prosecution on Wednesday, the 24th of August, at 7.15 p.m., that the next witness, who was to be DST-030, would not be coming to testify the following week. Just a day prior, the Defence had informed the Prosecution that we could anticipate receiving the 92 ter statement for DST-030 very soon. Until that point, the Prosecution was heavily engaged in preparatory work for DST-030 and DST-042. The ISU Unit was engaged; the Translation Unit informed of the prioritisation of documents pertaining to DST-030 from his ISU search. Rule 66(B) disclosure requests were being prepared. Rule 70 providers were contacted in relation to restricted documents in the ISU search results, and the team itself focussed all its work on DST-030. Following that, the team would turn to DST-042. When DST-030's testimony was postponed, the Defence informed us of their plan to call DST-040, who was scheduled to be the third witness following DST-030. The Prosecution does very much appreciate the Defence providing the draft statement of DST-040 that same evening, as well as their preliminary documents list containing approximately 236 documents. The Prosecution would note, however, that the draft statement provided to the Prosecution was compiled to a certain extent on dates in 2009 and 2010. Therefore, this draft statement could have been provided to the Prosecution by one week prior to the commencement of the Defence case, as we submit, was required pursuant to Rule 67(A)(ii). The change in the witness orders implicates not only the Prosecution's preparation for the witness but it has other implications which cause something of a domino effect on other units in the Tribunal as well. The last-minute change affects the timing of the ISU searches for this witness, the consequent Rule 70 clearance requests, the shifting of priorities for translation, and the responses from RFAs to Serbia. We made those shifts urgently on Friday to the best of our ability. In that context, the Prosecution notified Serbia that DST-040 will be testifying next week, that is, this week. And Serbia expedited the response to the RFA in respect of DST-040. The expedited response was provided. I would note that is only partially responsive to our request. It was provided on Monday, the 29th of August, at the close of business, containing 681 pages. Upon a brief view of those documents, they are directly and centrally relevant to the credibility of the witness. Just prior to that, the Prosecution had also received the RFA response in relation to DST-063 who is currently on the stand. That response contained 150 pages. One very serious concern is that the RFA responses which we receive, including these and others, are redacted in ways which impact upon the substance. In particular, names are redacted which could be highly relevant to our case. I will just show Your Honours one example. It's not from these two witnesses, but it's from another RFA response relevant to the case, and this -- these very extensive redactions that I've shown you --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Marcus, for the record, you've shown us one piece of paper with some five squares covering approximately a third of the surface of that piece of paper fully in black. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. The Prosecution may be seeking to engage the Chamber on this matter which we feel impacts upon Serbia's co-operation with the Tribunal. With respect to this, the Prosecution puts on the record that for any witnesses whose RFA responses from Serbia contain substantive redactions we may be seeking leave to re-call those witnesses once we are able to review the unredacted versions. In the mean time, additional language resources were requested and some language staff had to work yesterday during the holiday on the response for the witness that's currently on the stand, DST-063. On Monday, the 29th of August, at 7.38 p.m., the Prosecution received the final statement for DST-040. At 10.08 p.m., we received the final list of documents, containing 127 documents. At 1.38 p.m. yesterday, the 30th of August, the Prosecution received the comments chart for DST-040 containing 56 documents. But this morning the Defence added a number of documents to his exhibit list yet again. Now, the Prosecution understands the challenges involved in calling witnesses. However, the Prosecution's ability to prepare has been severely hampered in the instant circumstances. The Stanisic Defence requested the adjournment and they also requested the shift in the witness schedule. Now they ask for the schedule to be adjusted yet again to add additional hearings. We submit that in light of the circumstances this would unfairly prejudice the Prosecution. Due to the fact that the Prosecution has had the final statement only three days prior to commencement of testimony, we are still unaware of whether his comments chart contains the final selected exhibits or only some of them, and due to the RFA response which contains 681 pages which cannot be processed in one week, the Prosecution requests that the schedule remain as it is and that cross-examination of DST-040 be conducted after the adjournment. This proposed solution would not result in any prejudice to the ability of the Defence to present its case. In addition, we request the Chamber to order the Defence to provide us with all draft statements of upcoming witnesses pursuant to Rule 67(A)(ii) to enable us to prepare for those witnesses' evidence during the adjournment. And finally, Your Honours, we request that the Defence confirm to us the order of witnesses to be called after the adjournment. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Ms. Marcus. Mr. Jordash, I'm looking at the clock. I do not know whether it would be good to ask you to answer, which would be a matter of one or two minutes only, or whether I would invite you to make brief submissions either in writing in an informal way and then we put that on the record or whether you would start tomorrow morning -- well, tomorrow afternoon, it would be, first, to address the matter. I'm just looking -- at the same time, I'm also aware that, of course, tomorrow afternoon means another day of uncertainty.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: The only problem I can envisage that if the Prosecution are right, in relation to this latest disclosure, and that it impacts upon their ability to cross-examine the witness, then -- and Your Honours agree with that, then it follows that it would impact upon our ability to lead the witness in direct. So it may be that leaving the argument until tomorrow might -- well, I'm thinking aloud. It could be level until tomorrow, but that certainly would be part of the submission.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I do not know whether I fully understand that it would impact on your ability to lead the witness in direct. Is that because the RFA information came so late? Is that what you're referring to?

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Well, one thing that I would want or prefer would be that the Prosecution indicate what it is within the RFA that makes it so difficult for them to cross-examine the witness. I'm -- at least generally speaking. Because we've gone through it and can't see what the problem is because most of it relates to the trial of a number of people for the killing of Djindjic in 2003. There's nothing in that RFA, as far as we can see, which relates to this trial. So perhaps we've missed something, and we'd like the Prosecution to identify it so we can all know what we're dealing with.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then I suggest that the first thing you would do is to spend ten minutes together and that you explain that the 750 pages -- and I might remember your words, Mr. Jordash, that 750 pages, just a couple of days is quite sufficient. If you know more or less what the problem is, that would be really sufficient. I will remember those words. I'll not hold them against you, but I'll not forget them. And perhaps you spend ten minutes on the matter together so that you convince Ms. Marcus that it's only the shopping lists of Mr. A, B, or C, or that it's just the hairdresser's invoices over two years. So that Ms. Marcus, tomorrow, could report to the Chamber that she agrees with you and that there's no reason to postpone the cross-examination. What I'm suggesting is that you try to find out what really that material is about and to see to what extent you could meet each other's concerns. And then the Chamber, of course, will finally decide on how we will proceed and whether we'll grant the request by Ms. Marcus. But it seems that some more homework needs to be done before the Chamber is fed with the right information to decide on the request, at least in the respect of the postponement of the cross-examination. We adjourn for the day. And we'll resume tomorrow, the 1st of September, at quarter past 2.00 in the afternoon, in this same courtroom, II.
